images.title: Sorting by sides
images.purpose: Show equilateral, isosceles and scalene triangles by how many sides are equal.
images.composition: Three triangles in a row with equal spacing, each with its name below, a tick-mark key on the sides and plenty of white space.
exact_structure: Left: an equilateral triangle (three equal sides), each side with one teal (#0072B2) tick mark.
Middle: an isosceles triangle with sides in the ratio 5, 5 and 8 (wide, low): the two equal slanting sides each carry one amber (#E69F00) tick mark, the base has none.
Right: a scalene triangle with sides in the ratio 5, 6 and 7: the shortest side has one reddish purple (#CC79A7) tick, the middle side two ticks, the longest side three ticks.
Right: a scalene triangle with sides in the ratio 5, 6 and 7, all three sides different, with no tick marks at all.
Under each triangle its name and a short count of its equal sides.
rejection: tick marks that do not match the equal sides
the isosceles triangle having three equal sides or the scalene one having two
images.takeaway: Equilateral has 3 equal sides, isosceles has 2 equal sides, and scalene has all sides different.
images.description: Three triangles with tick marks: equilateral, isosceles and scalene.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Count the matching ticks on each triangle before reading the name.

image_decisions.why: Sorting by sides is a count of equal sides.
